newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Pound may dampen BTP profit rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pound may dampen BTP profit rise.

text.p: Specialty chemicals group BTP Plc said on Monday continued pound strength may shave a couple of millions of sterling off its full-year profit, which is still expected to show a strong rise.
"If it stays at its current level than we are probably looking at two million pounds off profits," chief executive Stephen Hannam told Reuters.
BTP earlier reported a 13 percent rise in its first-half pre-tax profit to 23.7 million stg from 21.0 million.
"It was another record six months because of organic growth and there 's more to come in the second half," said Hannam.
Continuing margin improvement due to less price pressure, as well as last year's investments, meant the group was in good shape, Hannam said.
"Even despite the currency we are finding life somewhat happier than last year," he said.
Lower raw material prices helped the adhesives and textile coatings division with operating profits up 45 percent to 3.05 million stg.
The safety equipment division, operating in markets growing by about 15 percent per year, saw profits climb to 4.85 million stg from 41.5 million.
Stronger government legislation was helping keep the outlook for the safety business bright, Hannam said. "We think we'll do rather well," he said.

Results in the biocides and fine chemicals division were boosted by strong performances of Nipa UK and Nipa Hardwicke USA. Results here will be helped by last year's investments in the insecticide business, where most sales take place in the second half of the year, BTP said.
The division's operating profit in the first half rose to 13.38 million stg from 11.45 million.

The performance chemicals division was hit by tough market conditions, particularly in Australia, but Hannam added that the division should benefit in the second half from a new chemicals plant coming onstream.
"A number of things have been done to improve things," he said.
Performance chemicals profits fell to 3.12 million stg from 3.72 million.
